**Sharing isn’t the only option. Programmatic access depends on the account type.**

| History | Available route |
|---|---|
| **Personal Claude chats** | Bulk export from **Settings → Privacy → Export data**. Claude emails a download link; we can then process the archive programmatically. [Official instructions](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9450526-export-your-claude-data) |
| **Personal ChatGPT chats** | I didn’t find a documented public API for retrieving personal chat history. An account data export, where available, is preferable to sharing conversations individually. |
| **ChatGPT Enterprise/Edu** | Eligible administrators can retrieve supported conversation records through the **Compliance API**. [Official documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/compliance-api) |
| **Claude Enterprise** | The **Compliance API** can list chats and retrieve messages using an appropriately scoped compliance key. A regular Claude API key is insufficient. [Official documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-content-data) |
| **Local coding-agent sessions** | Programmatic collection works—we already collected those logs. |

For this project, **bulk exports are the best next input for personal web-chat histories**. We can automate project filtering, deduplication, and integration into the report afterward.

One distinction matters: conversation text supports turn counts and steering analysis, but **exact input/output/cache tokens require usage metadata**. We should keep missing token usage marked unknown rather than estimate it as exact.

The online comparison suggests that the next additions should connect **activity to decisions and verified outcomes**, rather than add more usage statistics.

| Priority | Additional analysis | What it would establish |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Deliverable and outcome ledger** | For each major task: requested result, resulting artifact, acceptance evidence, remaining limitations, and rework. This connects AI activity to what the project actually achieved. |
| 2 | **Decision provenance** | Who proposed important choices, what alternatives were considered, whether the user accepted or challenged them, and what evidence changed the decision. This would examine influence in both directions. |
| 3 | **Correction effectiveness** | Whether each correction was acknowledged, implemented, verified, or later repeated. Include unresolved cases and distinguish agent mistakes from changed requirements. |
| 4 | **Verification quality** | Separate assistant-reported success from test output, independent review, artifact inspection, and user acceptance. Track regressions and cases where checks passed but the deliverable failed. |
| 5 | **Coordination and rework costs** | Identify duplicate work, stale information, handoffs, repeated explanations, and abandoned approaches. Attribute usage to work phases where the evidence permits. |

Several comparable reports explain why these matter:

- **OpenAI’s harness-engineering account** emphasizes delivered software, feedback loops, and converting human review into persistent repository rules. For Venn, a useful question is whether a correction became a reusable test or instruction—or had to be repeated. [Report](https://openai.com/index/harness-engineering/)
- **Anthropic’s compiler project** describes how verifier quality and task independence determined whether parallel agents made useful progress. **Cursor’s account** documents coordination bottlenecks and work churning without progress. These support examining productive parallelism separately from overlapping activity. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-c-compiler), [Cursor](https://cursor.com/blog/scaling-agents)
- **Anthropic’s judgment study** found that agents could substantially influence experts’ choices. That makes decision provenance particularly valuable: the report should document both effective human steering and consequential AI suggestions the user adopted. [Study](https://www.anthropic.com/research/agents-judgment-calls)
- **METR’s methodology update** highlights problems measuring task time when developers use concurrent agents. It supports retaining the report’s distinction between observed activity windows and actual effort. [Update](https://metr.org/blog/2026-02-24-uplift-update/)

My recommendation is to do **the outcome ledger and decision provenance first**. Together, they would make the report substantially stronger as an account of how human judgment and AI work produced the project.
